title: swarm:escalation:v1
description:
A lane-channel card for one of three distinct daemon events, discriminated by `cause`. The three were collapsed into one marker by APPENDIX-NORMATIVE.md section 3; this schema keeps them separable so a renderer never has to guess which shape it holds.

cause=concentration_crossing carries RuntimeEvent::Escalation (runtime_events.rs:290-299). cause=mode_transition carries RuntimeEvent::ModeTransition (:300-306) and is published ONLY for a transition INTO incident. cause=tamper_fail_closed carries RuntimeEvent::TamperAlert (:249-256) and is published ONLY when fail_closed is true.

Tier 0. None of the three carries a signature.

issuer.description: WHO PRODUCED THE FACT. See the envelope's `issuer` for who published it.

emitted_at_ms.description: The RuntimeEvent's own emitted_at_ms, carried through unchanged. THE SORT KEY for every Perch surface. The Nostr event's `created_at` is a transport timestamp stamped at publish, because MAX_TIMESTAMP_DRIFT_SECS is 900 and REJECTS (crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/ingest.rs:2224-2231) and `created_at` is inside the Nostr signature, so a spooled card carrying its true emit time becomes permanently unpublishable fifteen minutes after it was produced.

case_channel.description: Set when this escalation promoted a case.

distinct_sources.description: RuntimeEvent::Escalation.distinct_sources, carried through unchanged. The COUNTING UNIT is in the sibling field; do not assume it.

source_ids.description: The strategy-scoped ids themselves, `{derived_identity}:{agent_id}:{strategy_id}`. NULL ON EVERY PHASE-1 CARD — see the sibling source_ids_absent_reason for why, and note that the absence is a NAMED STATE, not a null a component may paper over. When B4 lands and the bridge can serve them, a consumer derives the agent half of render law 2 by dropping the last colon-separated segment (`id.split(':').slice(0, -1).join(':')`) and counting the distinct remainder. That derivation is correct ONLY under the strategy-scoped mechanism, which is why the mechanism is on the wire beside it.

dedupe_key.description: {threat_class_slug}:{level}:{unix_seconds}. The monitor is LEVEL-triggered at 10 Hz (CONCENTRATION_MONITOR_INTERVAL_MS=100, crates/swarm-runtime-http/src/bin/swarm_detect.rs:40) and evaluate_threat_class (crates/swarm-runtime/src/escalation.rs:61-103) has no memory of prior state, so it re-emits while over threshold; but `now` is unix_timestamp_secs (escalation.rs:407-410), so all ten ticks in a second are byte-identical. The bridge dedupes on this key and then EDGE-TRIGGERS on a level change. Without both steps twelve classes over threshold produce up to 120 events/second against a 120/min relay write quota.

source_ids_absent_reason.description: REQUIRED, and exactly one of this field and source_ids is null. Non-null names why the ids are missing so a surface renders that reason; null means source_ids is populated. Without this field the M half of render law 2 has no representable absence and every component that must show it either fabricates a number or spins.

allOf.title: exactly one of source_ids / source_ids_absent_reason is null

triggering_threat_class.description: Null on a de-escalation: transition_down clears it (crates/swarm-core/src/agent.rs:148-155). A card with to=incident always has it set, because transition_to requires it (:137-146).

unexpected_library_sha256.description: sha256 over the newline-joined, lexicographically sorted `unexpected_library_loads` list. Lets two alerts be compared for identity without the paths crossing a global frame. The paths themselves ARE on this durable lane card (see `details` and `unexpected_library_loads`) because a lane channel is membership-gated; they are NOT on the global 26005 frame.

unexpected_library_loads.description: RuntimeEvent::TamperAlert.unexpected_library_loads verbatim (runtime_events.rs:253). Host filesystem paths. Present on this card, absent from kind 26005.
